intro.heading: If you're planning a move to Spain, securing the right visa is your first essential step.
intro.subheading: Most expats relocate under one of two primary options: the Non-Lucrative Visa (NLV) or the Digital Nomad Visa (DNV).

whoCanApply.heading: Who can apply for the Non-Lucrative visa?

personas.label: People with large savings who do not need to work
People not working for their first year before applying for work permit

items.text: for one year, with renewals granted in two-year periods.
— apply for permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years of continuous legal residence.
— spouse or partner and dependent children can be included.
— spend up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the 26 Schengen countries.
— unlike other visas, there's no obligation to purchase property or invest in a business.

items.bold: Ideal for retirees or passive income earners
items.text: — well suited for those living off savings, pensions, or income from abroad.
— while employment with a Spanish company isn't permitted, education options remain open.

requirements.heading: What are the requirements for the Non-Lucrative Visa?

items.text: — you'll need to show stable savings or passive income to support yourself (and any dependents) without working in Spain.
— full-coverage Spanish health insurance with no co-payments is required for the duration of your stay.
items.italic: We partner with ASSA, a health insurance provider specifically for expats with exactly the right coverage to satisfy the visa requirements.

items.text: — background checks from your country (or countries) of residence for the past five years.
— confirmation that you do not have any illnesses that pose a public health risk under international regulations.
— this visa is designed for those who will not work for a Spanish employer.
— the initial application must be submitted through the Spanish consulate where you legally reside.
items.italic: Our team at Hola España handles the document preparation and coordinates the submission process, so everything is organized, accurate, and stress-free from start to finish.

whoCanApply.heading: Who can apply for the Digital Nomad visa?

personas.label: People who can perform their work fully online

items.bold: Live and work remotely from Spain
items.text: — legally reside in Spain for 1-3 years while continuing your professional activity with foreign clients or employers.
— after 5 years of legal residence, you may apply for long-term residency.
— spouse or partner and dependent children can be included.
— spend up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the 26 Schengen countries.
— unlike other visas, there's no obligation to purchase property or invest in a business.
— many applicants may qualify for Spain's special expat tax regime, depending on their situation.

requirements.heading: What are the requirements for the Digital Nomad Visa?

items.text: — employment contract, freelance agreements, or proof of business ownership showing you work with non-Spanish companies or clients.
— full-coverage Spanish health insurance with no co-payments is required for the duration of your stay.
items.italic: We partner with ASSA, a health insurance provider specifically for expats with exactly the right coverage to satisfy the visa requirements.

items.text: — background checks from your country (or countries) of residence for the past five years.
— confirmation that you do not have any illnesses that pose a public health risk under international regulations.
— you must meet the required monthly income level set by Spanish immigration authorities (higher amounts apply if including dependents).
— a university degree, professional certification, or at least three years of relevant work experience.
— whether applying from your home country or from within Spain can impact your approval timeline and residency length.
items.italic: Our team at Hola España manages the document preparation and guides you through the entire submission process, ensuring everything is structured correctly and handled smoothly.
